bm_p1.message: Bookmarks are usually not necessary when you can just Alt+U an unloaded tab you want to come back to later.

bm_p2.message: However, sometimes a bookmark can still be useful. Bookmarks provide a consistent starting point which does not change if you navigate to another page. You open it, navigate however you like, and the bookmark stays the same so you can start from the same page next time.

bm_p3.message: This is helpful when a site requires you to log in every day, so you can bookmark the login page and then immediately navigate away to some other page. Or if you frequently check a news site, and want to always start on the front page, but also want to go to other pages without opening new tabs. Or if you otherwise want to lock a saved tab so the URL and title won't change while you're browsing.

bm_p4.message: Bookmarks in TKTSTO are essentially the same as an unloaded tab, except for a few small differences:

bm_li2.message: When loaded, it opens as a new node, leaving the bookmark itself unchanged. The new node will be the first child of the bookmark node.

bm_make_heading.message: There are two ways to make a bookmark:

bm_make_li1.message: Press Alt+B (or Alt+K in Firefox) to bookmark the current tab. This will create a new bookmark node and make it the parent of the current tab's node.

bm_make_li2.message: Press E or click E in the hover menu to Edit Node on an unloaded tab in the Tree View, then set its "Bookmark?" checkbox and save the changes. This converts an unloaded tab into a bookmark.

bm_tip1.message: Tip: If you want a tab to open next to the current tab instead of opening as a child of a bookmark node, just middle click the node. This works for any tab node, not just bookmarks. Because tab nodes are links. You can middle click any tab node, whether loaded or unloaded, to open that node's URL in a new tab, and it will be placed the same as if you middle-clicked a link in the current page. So every tab node can be used like a native browser bookmark, even if it doesn't have a bookmark icon in the Tree View.

bm_tip2.message: Another tip: When you open a bookmark in the Tree View, the bookmark's mtime gets updated. It also gets updated when you close-and-delete the clone it spawned. This provides an easy way to automatically track when you last used a bookmark. Just enable the Details panel in the Tree View and check the mtime. Pretty handy if you have a news site bookmarked, and you want to know how far back to read before you'll get to articles you've already seen. Just be sure to check the mtime before you open the bookmark.

bm_ex_p1.message: Bookmark usage is pretty simple. For example, let's say you have a page open and you hit Alt+B (or Alt+K in Firefox) to bookmark the current page:

bm_ex_p2.message: A new bookmark node is created as a clone of the page you currently have focused. Then the focused page node is moved to become the bookmark's first child.

bm_ex_p3.message: Note: It does not matter where the Tree View cursor is. The Alt+B action applies to the page you have focused in the browser, not the tree view cursor node.

bm_ex_p4.message: Let's say you then decide to bookmark "Hacker News" too. But it isn't currently open. So use a different method:

bm_ex_p5.message: Put the Tree View cursor on it and press E, or click E in the hover menu to Edit Node. Then click the "Bookmark?" checkbox and save your changes.

bm_ex_p6.message: Afterward, double click it or press Enter on it to open the bookmark. Here's how the TreeView looks after each step:

bm_ex_p7.message: The "Hacker News" saved tab was first converted to a bookmark, then opened. The new page opens as its first child, and is Bold because it is now the focused page.

bm_ex_p8.message: One other detail to note: The bookmark icon changes color depending on whether there are any loaded tabs in the branch. This makes it easier to find open tabs, even if the bookmark branch is collapsed.

bm_native_p1.message: The browser's built-in bookmarks are not supported yet. TKTSTO provides a separate, alternate bookmark system, so you can more easily take your bookmarks with you if/when you change browsers, and not have to rely on a "Sign in to Chrome" type feature to sync between browsers.

bm_native_p2.message: However, a future version of TKTSTO may add some type of support for native bookmarks... at least enough to import them into the session tree.

bm_native_p3.message: A future version may also potentially add support for the "omnibar", to suggest TKTSTO bookmarks related to the current window.

cb_p1.message: Expand the "Checkboxes" branch if you haven't already. Looks like somebody is doing some grocery shopping... but they didn't organize their list yet! Let's help them out, and try 3 different ways of moving nodes around.

cb_li1.message: First, try using the mouse to drag the "Milk" item into the "Cold aisle" branch.

cb_li2.message: Second, press the Up arrow a few times to move the cursor to "Crackers". Then press Shift+Down to move it down a row or two. It should now be in the "Dry / Canned" branch.

cb_li3.message: Third, mark the nodes for "Ice cream" and "Popsicles", since they both need to be frozen. You can mark them by pressing the M button in the hover menu, or by pressing the M key while the cursor is on those rows. Then move the cursor down to "Frozen" and press P to paste. Then press Shift+M to unmark them.

cb_p2.message: That just leaves "Soup" remaining to be sorted. Use whatever method you like.

cb_p3.message: Then you remember you also need butter. Put the cursor somewhere in the "Cold aisle" branch and press the o key to open a new node on a new row. It'll ask you for a label, so type in "Butter" and press Enter. (the o and Shift+O keys are mapped by default to "addNodeAsNextVisibleRow" and "addNodeAsPrevVisibleRow", which match the keys used in Vim, a popular editor)

cb_p4.message: But "Butter" doesn't have a checkbox like all the other items.

cb_p5.message: To add a checkbox, you can either press the T key or click the T button in the hover menu. This brings up the "taskEdit" dialog.

cb_p6.message: Next, either click on the style of checkbox you want, or press a key on the keyboard with a printable letter on it. It can be any letter or symbol, so you can assign your own meanings to different symbols. For a simple "todo" checkbox, just press Space.

cb_quick_p1.message: For quick edits, put the cursor on a row and then press a short key sequence, like t and then Space to add a "todo" checkbox... or tx to mark a task as "done". Or t then Backspace to remove the checkbox. (t then Delete also works)

cb_quick_p2.message: Maybe you already have cheese, for example. Everyone should have cheese, which is why it is marked as "important". But you're a hoopy frood who already has some. So move the cursor to "Cheese" and type tx to mark it as "done". Note how the percent boxes change in response to this.

cb_types_p1.message: There are a few other types of tasks pre-defined...

cb_types_li1.message: The "percent" checkboxes calculate their own number if they have any children with checkboxes. Otherwise, you can set the value manually by typing something like t42 for 42% or t07 for 7%.

cb_types_li2.message: To set a priority of 1 to 9 instead, try t3 then press Enter to set a task to priority 3.

cb_types_li3.message: A "ratio" checkbox works a lot like a "percent" checkbox, except it displays a count of completed vs total child tasks, like 3/7 if you had 3 tasks done out of 7 total. Sometimes it's nice to have a counter instead of a percent.

cb_ex_text.message: Here is an example tree with a variety of checkbox types in it:

cb_footer.message: But you can use any printable character as the checkbox type. You can also get a lower-case task status by holding Shift when typing a letter.

tgt_title.message: Grey text is an unloaded tab

tgt_heading.message: Grey text is an unloaded tab.

tgt_p1.message: But now that you've opened it, the text probably changed color and became bold, because it is open and "active". Open tabs are shown in a brighter color than saved tabs, and the browser's current tab is shown in bold.

tgt_p2.message: And the sidepanel's cursor probably greyed out too, to show that the panel no longer has keyboard focus.

tgt_p3.message: Try clicking between this page and the sidepanel a few times to see how the colors change as focus moves.

tgt_p4.message: Then try unloading this page. There are a few ways to do this:

tgt_li1.message: Press Alt+U to unload the current page.

tgt_li2.message: Hover the mouse over a node in the sidepanel and click the U button in the "hover menu".

tgt_li3.message: Put the treeView (sidepanel) cursor on a node and press the U key on the keyboard.

tgt_li4.message: Or just close the page normally. It has a note attached, so it is "interesting" and will be saved automatically. Any node with a label, note, or checkbox is considered "interesting", and is kept in the tree when its browser tab is closed.

tgt_p5.message: Any time you unload a tab, it will be kept in the tree session in the sidepanel. You can open it again later to continue where you left off.

tgt_p6.message: For reference, when you close a tab, using regular browser actions like Ctrl+W or by clicking the tab's "X" button in the tab bar, the result depends on that tab's metadata in the tree session:

tgt_li5.message: If the tab has any metadata attached, like a label or note or checkbox, it will be saved. That means the tab is "interesting", and won't be deleted when you close the tab.

tgt_li6.message: If the tab has any interesting children, the tab will be saved. So if any child node has a label, note, or checkbox... the parent will be saved when closed. This applies to direct children only, not grandkids.

tgt_li7.message: If the tab is "boring" and it has no "interesting" children, it will be deleted from the tree session when the tab is closed. And if it has any children, they will be promoted to the parent's position in the tree.

wlt_p1.message: It means the tab was loaded when your session was saved, or when a window was last closed. When you open a saved window, all the pink wasLoaded tabs will be opened automatically and become loaded tabs. The regular grey unloaded tabs (like bookmarks) will not be opened automatically.

wlt_p2.message: So if you didn't change anything, this window should have only one tab open. The "Pink text ..." tab should be open, while the "Grey text ..." tab is not.

wlt_p3.message: This means you can save and restore windows (close and re-open) with just a click or two. I think that's pretty neat.

wlt_p4.message: By the way, this would be a good time to try clicking the button in the upper left corner of the sidepanel. It should say "Session" or "Window".

wlt_p5.message: That's the "viewScope" button, or the "Session / Window" button. It changes how much of the tree is visible in the current window's sidepanel. I keep most of my windows in "Window" mode so I can focus on one window at a time. But sometimes it's useful to switch to a full session view, for larger session management tasks, like moving windows around or re-opening saved windows.

wlt_p6.message: Anyway, when you're done reading this, try closing this window. There are a few ways to do it:

wlt_li1.message: Click the "X" button on the top right corner of the browser window. Depending on your computing environment, this button may or may not exist. Just close it like you would close any other window. Another popular method is Alt+F4.

wlt_li2.message: Some browsers have a hotkey to close a window, like Shift+Ctrl+W.

wlt_li3.message: Hover the mouse over the window row in the tree view, and click the U button (Unload) in the hover menu.

wlt_li4.message: With the sidepanel focused, and the cursor on the tree row, press the U key on the keyboard.

wlt_li5.message: With the cursor on the tree row, press the Alt+U key on the keyboard. This works even if the sidepanel isn't focused, using the browser's extension shortcuts feature.

wlt_p7.message: When you close a browser window, it is always saved in the tree unless it's "boring" (has no metadata) and completely empty. So don't be shy about closing windows when you're not using them. You can get them back later.

wlt_p8.message: Oh, and if you want to change a tab between "unloaded" and "wasLoaded" states, just keep pressing the U button. This lets you manually set which tabs will be auto-loaded when you open the window.

nt_props.message: Every node can have a label, note, checkbox, and children.

nt_branch_def.message: A branch is simply a node with children. It can be any node type.

nt_leaf_def.message: A leaf is a node with no children.

nt_states.message: Every branch can be expanded or collapsed, and every node can be marked and/or have the cursor on it.

nt_dividers_def.message: A blank row is just a label with a Space inside. A divider is just a label with a - or = inside.

nt_explain_intro.message: Some types may require additional explanation:

nt_wasloaded_explain.message: wasLoaded tabs are documented in more detail in the dedicated wasLoaded help page.

nt_discarded_explain.message: Discarded tabs are tabs that the browser has partially unloaded (suspended/hibernated). They still appear in the browser's tab bar. Focusing one reloads it.

nt_hidden_explain.message: Hidden tabs exist in Firefox-based browsers. They are not displayed in the browser's tab bar, but behave like regular tabs.

nt_empty_explain.message: An empty node is a label node with no label text. It shows the node ID instead.

nt_org_intro.message: The session tree can mostly be organized however you want, but there are a few restrictions:

nt_org_li1.message: The root node cannot be moved or deleted.

nt_org_li2.message: Loaded tabs must be inside a window node.

nt_org_li3.message: Loaded tabs cannot be moved between a regular window and an incognito window.

nt_org_li4.message: A loaded window node cannot be converted into a non-window node unless it is nested inside another window node with the same incognito status.

nt_org_li5.message: The Pinned branch is special and cannot be moved while it contains any loaded tabs.

nt_org_li6.message: Native browser tab groups cannot contain other tab groups (nesting tab groups is not allowed by the browser).

us_p1.message: In the "user styles" config option, you can enter any CSS you want, to change the appearance of the Tree Views and other TKTSTO pages.

us_p2.message: For example, this is what someone might write there to modify a few relatively simple things...

us_li1.message: make rows light up purple when the mouse passes over them

us_li3.message: increase the spacing between rows a little bit

us_li4.message: make stuff move around less during a drag-n-drop

us_p3.message: To see what specific stylings might be useful to override, take a look at the default theme base, the night theme, and the day theme. Particularly the parts at the bottom, inside of :root { ... } because those variables are relatively easy to modify.

us_p4.message: ... and if you make a cool theme, send it in so it can be included for everyone else to use! <3

pt_intro.message: Pinned tabs are supported, and get pinned (or unpinned) by moving them into (or out of) a special branch called "Pinned" at the top of a window.

pt_how_heading.message: To pin or unpin a tab:

pt_method1.message: Use the browser's native functions: Right click a tab in the browser's tab bar. In the pop-up menu, click the "Pin" or "Unpin" option. The tab should become pinned (or unpinned), along with all its child tabs.

pt_method2.message: Move nodes in the Tree View: Use TKTSTO's sidepanel to move nodes or branches into or out of the Pinned branch. The browser's internal pinned state will update accordingly.

pt_recommendation.message: The TKTSTO Tree View will generally be more reliable than the browser's native functions, so I recommend doing it that way in most cases.

pt_native_p1.message: Let's say you want to pin a tab called "Pin Me!". Right click on that tab in the browser's native tab bar, then click "Pin".

pt_anchor_explain.message: Note how a new node was created, called Pinned. This node is special. It cannot be moved while it has loaded tabs, so it has an anchor icon next to it. It is locked in place at the top of the window.

pt_children_pinned.message: All the children of "Pin Me!" got pinned too. The nested branch structure is preserved.

pt_unpin_intro.message: If you change your mind and want to unpin it, right click on the "Pin Me!" tab again and click "Unpin":

pt_unpin_explain.message: The entire branch gets unpinned. And since the "Pinned" branch no longer has loaded tabs inside, its icon changes to a thumbtack icon.

pt_tktsto_p1.message: If you have no "Pinned" branch yet, make one. Put the cursor on the window node, expand it, then press o to add a new node and set its label to "Pinned".

pt_tktsto_p2.message: Then move nodes or branches into or out of the Pinned branch. The browser's internal pinned state and tab bar will update accordingly.

pt_unpin_all.message: If you want to unpin everything, simply delete the "Pinned" node while it is expanded, or change its name.

pt_vivaldi_issue.message: Vivaldi has special behavior when closing windows with pinned tabs. Using TKTSTO's Unload button to close windows in Vivaldi avoids losing pinned tab metadata.

src_intro.message: To search the tree, a few commands are available:

src_cmd1.message: / : Start a search, or re-focus the search bar during a search.

src_cmd2.message: Shift+* : Start a search for anything matching the current node's label, title, url, or note. Returns focus to the tree view immediately.

src_cmd3.message: Enter while the search bar is focused: Give focus back to the TreeView, and keep the search active. Can also just click in the TreeView to focus it.

src_cmd4.message: N / Shift+N : Go to the next (or previous) match.

src_cmd5.message: M / Shift+M / P : Mark the current node, unmark all nodes, or paste all marked nodes.

src_cmd6.message: Escape : End or cancel the search.

src_cmd7.message: Escape (again): Close any branches which were temporarily expanded to show hidden nodes.

src_workflow.message: One common workflow is to find everything matching a given query, then pull them all together into one place. To do this, type /foo to do a search for "foo", then press Enter to go back to the TreeView. Press n and m repeatedly to go to the next match and mark it. Then move the cursor to the place where you want all those nodes to be, and press p to paste everything. Finally, Shift+M to unmark everything, and Escape once or twice to cancel the search.

src_terms_p1.message: Searches look through all of a node's attached data. In particular, it checks the label, title, url, and note. If you don't see why a particular node was included as a match, open the details box to see more of the data it searched through.

src_terms_p2.message: Searches are made of one or more search terms, separated by spaces. Results only include nodes which match all search terms. Searches are not case sensitive. Each individual term is a regular expression.

src_terms_p3.message: The full scope of what regular expressions can do is way more than we can cover here, but here are a few simple tricks:

src_regex2.message: \. matches a literal . character, and also works to escape other special symbols.

src_regex3.message: x* matches any number of x characters, like ab*c matches abc, abbbbbbc, and ac.

src_regex4.message: x+ matches one or more x characters.

src_regex5.message: x? matches zero or one of x, making it optional.

src_regex6.message: x{n,m} matches at least n instances of "x", and up to m.

src_regex7.message: ^foo matches "foo" at the beginning of a string.

src_regex8.message: foo$ matches "foo" at the end of a string.

src_regex9.message: [abc] matches any of the characters inside brackets (e.g. [a-z]).

src_regex10.message: [^abc] matches anything except the characters inside brackets.

src_regex13.message: \x matches a predefined character class (\d for digits, \w for word chars, \s for whitespace).

src_ex1.message: face.*mess matches anything containing "face" and then "mess", such as "Facebook Messenger".

src_footer.message: But most of the time, you probably won't need more than just a simple word or two, to find what you're looking for.

fto_intro.message: If you're migrating from Tabs Outliner, there are a few things which would be helpful to know.

fto_dt_p1.message: Back up your data in Tabs Outliner first. Do an export or backup if you can... and if not, at least do an "expand all nodes" and then Ctrl+S to save the page.

fto_dt_p2.message: The backup files are in .json format, and can be imported into TKTSTO directly. However, you may need to rename the backup file extension from .tree to .json before importing it.

fto_dt_p3.message: Saved session view pages can be converted to a usable format using an extra script called bin/tabs-outliner-html-to-tktsto-json.py in the TKTSTO repository.

fto_dt_p4.message: Once you have a backup file in .json format, import it into TKTSTO via the Options page -> Import section.

fto_free_heading.message: Doing a Tabs Outliner backup when you have the free version

fto_free_intro.message: Daniel contributed this handy tip for exporting backups without paying for Premium Mode in Tabs Outliner:

fto_free_step1.message: open the options page in Tabs Outliner

fto_free_step3.message: right click in the whitespace somewhere on the page and select "Inspect".

fto_free_step4.message: the developer tools will open on the "Elements" tab.

fto_free_step5.message: find the element with id "licenseKeyPresentBackupTabBlock" (which has style="display: none;").

fto_free_step6.message: double click display: none to edit and delete that text.

fto_free_step7.message: The backup options will now appear on the page.

fto_free_step8.message: Click "Export Tree to File" to create your backup.

fto_free_step10.message: Now you can import the backup into TKTSTO.

fto_sv_p1.message: Tabs Outliner forced users to keep a separate window open for the session tree. TKTSTO can work that way, but provides a better built-in sidepanel workflow.

fto_sv_p2.message: Instead of keeping a separate window open for the session view, reclaim that space and use TKTSTO's sidepanel (Alt+T in Chrome, F1 in Firefox). In "Window" mode, it automatically displays only the active window's tabs.

fto_sv_p3.message: To move items between windows, use "mark and paste" (M to mark, P to paste), which is much faster and easier than drag-and-drop between separate windows.

fto_mk_p1.message: Unlike Tabs Outliner, TKTSTO keyboard shortcuts are 100% free and not locked behind a paywall. Using the keyboard for tree management is strongly recommended.

fto_hm_p1.message: TKTSTO has a hover menu similar to Tabs Outliner, but rearranged to prevent accidental deletion. It automatically hides when using the keyboard.

mn_p1.message: There are three ways to move nodes or branches around:

mn_dnd_p1.message: Drag & Drop: Grab a node with the mouse, press and hold the left mouse button, then move the mouse cursor around. Drag to the right side of a node to place it as a child. Drag to the left side to place it as a next sibling.

mn_hk_p1.message: Hotkeys: Put the cursor on a node in the sidepanel, then hold Shift and press the Arrow keys to move the node around. Use Shift+Left twice to promote a node out of a branch. (Requires Session view mode to move across windows).

mn_mp_p1.message: Mark & Paste: Press M on the keyboard or click the M button to mark a node. Mark as many nodes as you like. Then move to the destination and press P to paste them. Press Shift+M to unmark everything when done.

mn_dnd_explain1.message: This is how things look when doing a drag-n-drop to the right side of a branch (becomes a child):

mn_dnd_explain2.message: Or drag-n-drop on the left side of a branch to make it a sibling of the target node:

mn_mp_explain1.message: Here's how it looks when doing a mark (M) and paste (P) instead...

mn_mp_explain2.message: To paste after a branch instead of inside it, collapse the target first (Space or click arrow). To paste before, press Shift+P.

mn_reorder_p1.message: Mark and paste is also a quick way to reorder nodes: mark them in the order you want them to appear, then paste.

fs_p1.message: Welcome to TK's Tree Style Tab Outliner (TKTSTO)! This page covers the basic concepts to help you get started quickly.

fs_panel_p1.message: TKTSTO operates primarily from your browser's side panel:

fs_panel_chrome.message: Chrome / Chromium / Edge / Brave: Press Alt+T or click the extension icon in your toolbar to toggle the side panel.

fs_panel_ff.message: Firefox / Floorp / Zen: Press F1 to open the sidebar.

fs_tutorial_p1.message: To start the built-in interactive tutorial at any time:

fs_tutorial_step.message: Focus the TKTSTO side panel by clicking inside it, then press the ? key on your keyboard.

fs_tutorial_p2.message: This will generate interactive tutorial nodes at the top of your session tree to guide you through basic tree manipulation.

fs_basic_unload.message: Unloading Tabs: Press Alt+U (or U when panel is focused) to unload an active tab. It stays saved in your tree so you can re-open it later without using RAM.

fs_basic_add.message: Adding Nodes: Press o to add a new label node below the cursor. Use labels, notes, and checkboxes to organize your workflow.

fs_basic_move.message: Moving Nodes: Use Shift+Arrow keys or click M to mark nodes and P to paste them into another location or window.

fs_basic_modes.message: Window vs Session Mode: Toggle between viewing only the current window or your entire multi-window session using the button at the top-left of the panel.

fs_footer.message: Explore the other help pages for more details on bookmarks, checkboxes, user styles, and migration!
